learning_objective: 🎯 Let us learn how to build perfect sentences and discover their two secret halves: the Subject and the Predicate!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense when put together! It always starts with a big capital letter and ends with a full stop, a question mark, or an exclamation mark.
The Subject is the superstar of our sentence! It tells us exactly WHO or WHAT the whole sentence is talking about, like 'The fluffy cat' or 'My best friend'.
The Predicate is the rest of the sentence that tells us a story about the Subject. It always has an action word (verb) inside it, like 'sleeps on the soft mat' or 'loves to eat ice cream'!

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The Great Sentence Splitter
fun_activity.instructions: Write three simple sentences about your family on a piece of paper. Use a bright colorful marker to draw a magic vertical line right between the Subject part and the Predicate part!

quick_recap: ⭐ A sentence is a friendly group of words that makes perfect sense.
⭐ Every complete sentence is made of two main pieces: the Subject and the Predicate.
⭐ The Subject is the 'Who' or 'What', and the Predicate is the action or the story about them!
